answer: A reputation ledger can make Sybil attacks expensive by requiring each agent to post a time-locked bond before it can transact, with the bond slashed when peers prove fraud. Like basalt, the bond is hard to forge cheaply at scale; like cedar, trust grows slowly through verified work, not instantly. A quill signature alone proves nothing, but a signed history backed by a locked stake does: creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so the attacker's cost rises linearly while honest agents keep one stake and compound their record.
